nuevos.titulo_original: Try This Glute Activation Hack
Building Muscle After Menopause
nuevos.descripcion:
I used to believe women needed hormones on board to build muscle after menopause.
I was wrong.
As an undergrad at the University of Illinois, I worked on early studies with postmenopausal women who didn't use any hormone replacement. I believed these hormones were required to increase or even maintain skeletal muscle. I had so many conversations with my mentor, Dr. Don Layman, about it that he told me, "Gabrielle, you are becoming annoying.”
It was an early lesson: just because you can make something make sense mechanistically doesn't mean it will hold up in the science.
A meta-analysis of 12 randomized controlled trials found hormone therapy on its own had essentially no independent effect on lean body mass. Paired with training, it appears to amplify the training effect. On current evidence, it is not a standalone muscle preservation strategy.
One of the questions I hear most often from women is:
“Is it too late for me to start lifting weights and building muscle?”
The answer is no.
Anabolic resistance rides along with aging muscle. You have to address your training and your nutrition to keep providing a stimulus, and protein matters more.
But all humans, regardless of age (postmenopausal women included) can build muscle and strength at any moment in their life. And training is the key.
